description: Treat Huffman decoding as a finite state machine (FSM) and parallelize it by speculatively executing from multiple possible start states simultaneously. Rather than guessing a single state (speculation) or trying all states (enumeration), select a small set of likely states based on statistical properties of the codebook.
mathematical_formalization: Huffman decoder FSM has states Q = {q_0, ..., q_m} where m = max code length. For chunk C_i starting at unknown state, enumerate candidate states Q_cand subset Q with |Q_cand| = E. Run E parallel decoders. After processing L bits, most candidates converge to the same state with probability p_converge ~ 1 - (1-1/|Q|)^L. Expected wasted work = E * (1 - 1/E) * L_converge.
analogical_connections: Protein folding: exploring multiple conformation paths simultaneously and pruning unlikely ones
Chess engine search: alpha-beta pruning explores multiple game trees in parallel
MicroSpec FSM parallelization: speculation-centric fine-grained parallelization
implementation_hypothesis: For a DEFLATE block with max code length 15, there are 15 possible FSM states (bit positions within a code). Use SIMD to run 8 or 16 speculative decoders simultaneously. After 64 decoded symbols, check for convergence (all candidates agree on output). On convergence, discard wrong candidates. On failure, fall back to sequential decode for that chunk.
experiment_seed: Implement enumerative speculation for DEFLATE Huffman decoding using AVX2 (8 candidates) and AVX-512 (16 candidates). Measure convergence rate, wasted work ratio, and net throughput improvement over sequential decode.
